messages:
Oliver H: Heads-up: replay vs synthetic benches are diverging on A100-80GB across our clusters. Need a short sync.
Maya S: What symptoms?
Oliver H: Replay shows ~7-10% lower tokens/s and 30-60ms higher p95 on long sequences compared to synthetic. Same model + batch config.
Zeynep K: Any kernel-selector differences? We saw non-deterministic picks across image builds last sprint.
Oliver H: Yes. Replay hosts choose 'attention_fallback' often; synthetic runs pick 'fused_attention_v2'.
Arthur L: That explains tails. Different kernels = different cache locality and memory traffic. Do we have NVTX or cuprof traces?
Oliver H: Quick samples attached inline. Node R (replay):
```
NVTX region: token_gen
avg token latency: 13.1ms
kernel: attention_fallback
sm_efficiency=66% mem_util=78%
```
Node S (synthetic):
```
NVTX region: token_gen
avg token latency: 11.8ms
kernel: fused_attention_v2
sm_efficiency=84% mem_util=60%
```
Maya S: Hardware + driver mismatch possibility. What are driver/CUDA/image details?
Oliver H: Node S: driver=525.89 CUDA=11.8 image=redwood/runtime:2026-03-02
Node R: driver=535.86 CUDA=12.1 image=redwood/runtime:2026-04-11
Zeynep K: cuBLAS dispatch changed between those drivers; kernel heuristics and epilog choices can differ. Also check libcuda vs vendor kernel module versions.
Arthur L: Also note CPU governor, PCIe settings, and whether NVLINK topology differs. MIG config could change scheduler behavior.
Maya S: Reproduce plan: swap images on same host to see if perf follows image or host. If it follows image, it's runtime/image flags; if host, driver/hw.
Oliver H: Did an image-swap quickcheck: parity improved but not fully. Forcing REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=attention_fallback on synthetic drops perf to replay levels.
Zeynep K: So kernel selection is the lever. We should run a parameter sweep: drivers [525.89, 530.41, 535.86], CUDA [11.8, 12.0, 12.1], images [2026-03-02, 2026-04-11], kernel_hint [auto, fused_attention_v2, attention_fallback]. Include MIG vs non-MIG and CPU governors.
Arthur L: Add host types A100-80 and H100 to catch arch differences. Also record container runtime args (RT_LOCKLESS, LD_PRELOAD, runc vs crun). Tiny run-to-run env bits caused flakiness before.
Maya S: Metrics to collect: tokens/s, p50/p95/p99, kernel selection histogram, NVTX timelines, cuprof summaries, and nsight sampling for worst combos.
Oliver H: Agree. Harnesses: replay (10k representative traces with original arrival times) and synthetic mixed-len continuous stress for 1h. Keep client-side jitter off for apples-to-apples.
Zeynep K: Add explicit runtime logging: emit chosen kernel name and selector rationale into the trace/span metadata so posthoc diffs are easy. I'll add that change and push a build.
CI Bot: perf-nightly job scheduled: perf-matrix/1819992500-env-parity-sweep -> queued. :white_check_mark:
Maya S: I'll prepare nsight sampling template and a perf collection playbook (commands to capture /proc/driver/nvidia/version, nvidia-smi csv output, dmesg tail, and docker run args).
Oliver H: Also capture `ldd` of runtime binary and `objdump -T` exports to detect ABI differences. Small C++ runtime ABI mismatches have bitten us.
Arthur L: For faster triage, add a small assertion in runtime that logs kernel name to stdout for every 1000th token generation so we can see distribution without full tracing.
Zeynep K: If the sweep points to a specific driver/CUDA combo regress, we'll open a vendor ticket and pin the conductor CI matrix to the previous working driver.
Oliver H: Action items in thread: (1) I run the 54-combo sweep across A100/H100 tonight. (2) Maya prepares perf collection and nsight scripts. (3) Zeynep lands kernel-selection logging. (4) Arthur adds CI coverage for top-3 combos.
Maya S: Quick repro commands I'm using:
```
# replay with recorded arrivals
python tools/replay_harness.py --trace sample_10k.json --arrival-mode recorded --out replay_metrics.json
# synthetic bench matching arrival pattern
python tools/synth_bench.py --arrival-pattern recorded --duration 3600 --out synth_metrics.json
```
Oliver H: I'll post CSVs and kernel histograms back here once sweep completes. Tagging the runtime commit SHA and kernel-selector binary in logs.
Zeynep K: If anyone sees opaque kernel choices, enable DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECTOR and include selector logs.
Arthur L: Good plan. Also remember to set kube node taints consistently so we don't accidentally hit autoscaler nodes with different config.
Oliver H: Starting sweep now. Will update. :rocket:
